rule: During the mileage ramp, every 4th normal week holds mileage flat (on top of scheduled deload weeks).
summary: Periodic reduced or held weeks are near-universal practice (strength athletes deload every ~5-6 weeks; a coaches' Delphi agrees on deloading but not on its timing), but no trial tests a 3:1 ramp/hold pattern for running injury or fitness. Frandsen 2025 found week-to-week mileage change unrelated to injury, so the hold week has no injury-prevention evidence; its cost is a slower ramp (about one week in four without growth). Cheap and conservative during a return to running; label as a heuristic.

sources.note: Delphi of strength/physique coaches: deloading endorsed; timing/frequency left to judgement
Survey: strength athletes deload every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks; practice, not outcome data
Week-to-week distance ratio not associated with overuse injury
